title: Gluing simplicial localizations across monomorphic pushout spans
statement: Use small simplicial sets, coherent functor categories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and localization at a collection of edges as defined in [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. Let $X_{01}\xrightarrow{u_0}X_0$, $X_{01}\xrightarrow{u_1}X_1$ and $Y_{01}\xrightarrow{v_0}Y_0$, $Y_{01}\xrightarrow{v_1}Y_1$ be spans, and let $p_{01},p_0,p_1$ be a strictly commuting map from the first span to the second. Suppose $u_0$ and $v_0$ are degreewise injective. For $i\in\{01,0,1\}$ let $V_i\subseteq(X_i)_1$ be a collection of edges such that $p_i:X_i\to Y_i$ exhibits $Y_i$ as a localization of $X_i$ at $V_i$. Assume $u_0(V_{01})\subseteq V_0$ and $u_1(V_{01})\subseteq V_1$. Form the degreewise pushouts $X=X_0\amalg_{X_{01}}X_1$, $Y=Y_0\amalg_{Y_{01}}Y_1$, write $j_i:X_i\to X$ for their structure maps, and let $p:X\to Y$ be induced by the $p_i$. Then $p$ exhibits $Y$ as a localization of $X$ at $j_0(V_0)\cup j_1(V_1)$. The simplicial sets need not be quasicategories, and the maps $p_i$, $u_1$, and $v_1$ need not be injective.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 6.3.5.3 (01N7), implication (1) to (2), specialized to ordinary pushouts along monomorphisms using Example 4.5.5.12 (01FJ). These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-17; archived source WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a quasicategory $\mathcal E$, enlarging the universe so that it and all the simplicial sets are small. For a degreewise pushout $K=B\amalg_A D$ of simplicial sets, $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ is the strict pullback $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal E)}\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal E)$ of the two restriction maps: in each degree, product with the set $(\Delta^n)_m$ preserves pushouts of sets, so $K\times\Delta^n=(B\times\Delta^n)\amalg_{A\times\Delta^n}(D\times\Delta^n)$, and a map out of it is exactly a pair of maps agreeing on $A\times\Delta^n$, compatibly with all simplicial operators. Apply this to $X=X_0\amalg_{X_{01}}X_1$ and to $Y=Y_0\amalg_{Y_{01}}Y_1$. Since $u_0$ and $v_0$ are degreewise injective, the restrictions $\operatorname{Fun}(X_0,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X_{01},\mathcal E)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(Y_0,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(Y_{01},\mathcal E)$ are isofibrations between quasicategories by the restriction clause of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] both strict pullback squares are pullback squares in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. (This is the categorical-pushout property of Kerodon Example 4.5.5.12 (01FJ) for the two squares.) No injectivity of $u_1$, $v_1$ or the $p_i$, and no quasicategory hypothesis on the $X_i,Y_i$, is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3, hypothesis (a) and the first sentence of the proof (homotopy pullback square of functor categories); Example 4.5.5.12 (01FJ) for the front square, which is what makes condition (1) hold.

proof.text: For $i=01,0,1$ let $\mathcal L_i\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(X_i,\mathcal E)$ be the full subcategory on diagrams carrying every edge of $V_i$ to an equivalence. A full subcategory of a quasicategory is a quasicategory, since an inner horn of dimension at least two contains all vertices of its simplex, so the ambient filler already lies in it. Because $u_0(V_{01})\subseteq V_0$ and $u_1(V_{01})\subseteq V_1$, restriction carries $\mathcal L_0$ and $\mathcal L_1$ into $\mathcal L_{01}$, giving a cospan $\mathcal L_0\to\mathcal L_{01}\leftarrow\mathcal L_1$. The left map is an isofibration. Inner horns lift by the ambient isofibration of Step 1 and fullness. For an equivalence edge $e:F\circ u_0\to G$ of $\mathcal L_{01}$ with $F\in\mathcal L_0$, the ambient isofibration gives an equivalence edge $\tilde e:F\to F'$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(X_0,\mathcal E)$ restricting to $e$. Its components $\tilde e_x$ are equivalences by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences]. For $w:x\to y$ in $V_0$, the square $\tilde e|_{w\times\Delta^1}$ gives $[F'(w)][\tilde e_x]=[\tilde e_y][F(w)]$ in $h\mathcal E$; the other three classes are invertible, so $F'(w)$ is an equivalence edge by the characterization in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Hence $F'\in\mathcal L_0$, and by fullness $\tilde e$ with its inverse witnesses lies in $\mathcal L_0$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3, hypotheses (b)-(d) (the inclusions G(W_01) in W_0, H(W_01) in W_1) and the proof step passing to the localized functor categories (via Proposition 3.4.1.16 there).

proof.text: Put $W=j_0(V_0)\cup j_1(V_1)\subseteq X_1$ and let $\mathcal L\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)$ be the full subcategory on diagrams inverting $W$. A diagram $F$ on $X$ inverts $j_i(w)$ exactly when $F\circ j_i$ inverts $w$, so under the strict identification of Step 1 an object lies in $\mathcal L$ exactly when its restrictions lie in $\mathcal L_0$ and $\mathcal L_1$ (and then its restriction to $X_{01}$ lies in $\mathcal L_{01}$ by Step 2). Since all these subcategories are full, membership of a simplex is decided by its vertices, so $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_0\times_{\mathcal L_{01}}\mathcal L_1$ as simplicial sets, compatibly with the projections. By the isofibration of Step 2 and [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit], this square is a pullback square in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3, the edge collection W = H'(W_0) union G'(W_1) and the homotopy pullback of the localized functor categories.

proof.text: Write $k_i:Y_i\to Y$ for the structure maps, so $p\circ j_i=k_i\circ p_i$. For $G:Y_0\to\mathcal E$ one has $(G p_0)u_0=(G v_0)p_{01}$, and similarly for $Y_1$; hence the functors $p_i^*$ commute strictly with the restriction maps. By the localization hypotheses and [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map], each $p_i^*:\operatorname{Fun}(Y_i,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal L_i$ is a functor equivalence. They form an objectwise equivalence of cospan diagrams by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences]. The induced map of the strict pullbacks is $p^*:\operatorname{Fun}(Y,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal L$, because the restrictions of $G\circ p$ are $(G k_i)\circ p_i$; in particular $p^*$ lands in $\mathcal L$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, component localization equivalences and the induced map of cospans.

proof.text: The square of $\operatorname{Fun}(Y,\mathcal E)$ is limiting by Step 1. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-of-cospan-limits] to the objectwise-equivalent cospan from Step 4 and using the cospan invariance and mapping-space naturality in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion], the map $p^*$ from this limiting cone to the limiting cone $\mathcal L$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\operatorname{Fun}(Y,\mathcal E))^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal L)^\simeq$ for every small quasicategory $Q$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, cospan-limit comparison and Proposition 6.3.1.13 mapping-space criterion.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-test-equivalence-by-functor-cores], the equivalences on all test cores make $p^*$ a functor equivalence onto $\mathcal L$. Since $W$ is independent of $\mathcal E$, the defining universal-localization condition in [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map] now says that $p$ exhibits $Y$ as a localization of $X$ at $j_0(V_0)\cup j_1(V_1)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3, implication (1) to (2), final universal-localization conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3, implication (1) to (2). The front square is categorical by Example 4.5.5.12 (01FJ), realized here by the isofibration and isofibration-pullback nodes. The proof is expanded through strict functor-category pullbacks along isofibrations and edge-inverting full subcategories. Archived source WANTED.

lean.statement: theorem localizationAtEdges_monomorphic_pushout {X₀₁ X₀ X₁ Y₀₁ Y₀ Y₁ : SSet.{u}} (u₀ : X₀₁ ⟶ X₀) (u₁ : X₀₁ ⟶ X₁) (v₀ : Y₀₁ ⟶ Y₀) (v₁ : Y₀₁ ⟶ Y₁) (p₀₁ : X₀₁ ⟶ Y₀₁) (p₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (p₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (h₀ : u₀ ≫ p₀ = p₀₁ ≫ v₀) (h₁ : u₁ ≫ p₁ = p₀₁ ≫ v₁) (hu₀ : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (u₀.app n)) (hv₀ : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (v₀.app n)) (V₀₁ : Set (X₀₁ _⦋1⦌)) (V₀ : Set (X₀ _⦋1⦌)) (V₁ : Set (X₁ _⦋1⦌)) (h₀₁ : IsLocalizationAtEdges.{u, v} p₀₁ V₀₁) (hV₀ : IsLocalizationAtEdges.{u, v} p₀ V₀) (hV₁ : IsLocalizationAtEdges.{u, v} p₁ V₁) (hV₀₁₀ : (u₀.app (Opposite.op ⦋1⦌)) '' V₀₁ ⊆ V₀) (hV₀₁₁ : (u₁.app (Opposite.op ⦋1⦌)) '' V₀₁ ⊆ V₁) : IsLocalizationAtEdges.{u, v} (pushout.map u₀ u₁ v₀ v₁ p₀ p₁ p₀₁ h₀ h₁) (((pushout.inl u₀ u₁).app (Opposite.op ⦋1⦌)) '' V₀ ∪ ((pushout.inr u₀ u₁).app (Opposite.op ⦋1⦌)) '' V₁)
lean.note: The theorem states the Kerodon 01N7 localization gluing property for degreewise pushouts. The only monomorphism hypotheses are hu₀ and hv₀; no quasicategory or extra injectivity assumptions are present.
